summary: This lecture covers Chapter 36 of Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, focusing on fasting in Ramadan and its spiritual purposes. Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains that fasting is one of the five pillars of Islam and discusses the etymology of Ramadan, clarifying that Islamic calendar names contain no elements of disbelief unlike Western calendar names rooted in mythology. The lecture emphasizes that the true purpose of fasting extends beyond merely abstaining from food and drink—it is about developing self-discipline, restraint from haram, empathy for the poor, and spiritual purification that restricts Satan's influence on the soul.
